angles.title: Assets fell, contributions did not
angles.core_message: In September 2026 SIP assets fell 4.1%, yet monthly SIP contributions still rose 0.6%.

key_points.text: SIP assets fell 4.1% to 17.86 lakh crore rupees in September 2026, mainly from market-value losses.
Monthly SIP contribution rose 0.6% to 32,490 crore rupees in the same month.
Contributing SIP accounts rose to 10.06 crore from 10.02 crore.

angles.audience: MFD explaining September 2026 SIP data to a worried SIP client
angles.why_now: September 2026 AMFI data is the latest published; October is not out yet. Carousel suits a three-number contrast.
out_of_scope: advice to start or stop a SIP
risks: No performance figure is shown, so no disclaimer is triggered; check at step 4.
AMFI does not explain why contributions rose, so the script must not say why.

angles.title: Same pattern, second time: March and September
angles.core_message: SIP assets fell in both March and September 2026, while monthly SIP contributions rose in both months.

key_points.text: March 2026: contribution rose 7.5% to 32,087 crore rupees while SIP assets fell 9.2%.
September 2026: contribution rose 0.6% to 32,490 crore rupees while SIP assets fell 4.1%.

angles.audience: MFD giving clients a longer view than one month
angles.why_now: A two-month comparison shows the pattern is not a one-off. Infographic suits side-by-side figures.
out_of_scope: advice to start or stop a SIP
risks: F007 is older than 120 days and is approved only as a dated comparison; show its date clearly.
Two data points are not a trend; the script must not call it one.

angles.title: Who is still in: accounts, new SIPs, discontinued SIPs
angles.core_message: In September 2026, 63.26 lakh new SIPs were registered and 49.68 lakh were discontinued or completed.

key_points.text: 63.26 lakh new SIPs were registered in September 2026.
49.68 lakh SIPs were discontinued or reached the end of their tenure.
Contributing SIP accounts stood at 10.06 crore.

angles.audience: MFD who wants a client-facing view of SIP participation
angles.why_now: Participation counts are the clearest answer to whether investors are staying invested.
out_of_scope: advice to start or stop a SIP
risks: The AMFI footnote on 'discontinued' was not read verbatim; the script may only state the two counts, and 'completed' must not be read as 'stopped early'.

angles.title: Why SIP exists: the AMFI explanation, plus September's numbers
angles.core_message: AMFI describes SIP as disciplined investing at regular intervals, and September 2026 contributions stayed above 32,000 crore rupees.

key_points.text: AMFI describes a SIP as investing a fixed amount at regular intervals instead of a lump sum.
AMFI says SIP supports rupee cost averaging and disciplined investing without timing the market.
September 2026 monthly SIP contribution was 32,490 crore rupees.

angles.audience: MFD explaining SIP basics to a first-time client during a volatile month
angles.why_now: Pairs the standard definition with the latest figure; low-risk and short.
out_of_scope: advice to start or stop a SIP
risks: Rupee cost averaging must be attributed to AMFI, not stated as a promise of better returns.
